title: Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, Revenue Recognition & Billing (2026 Appendix)
author: Claire Morgan
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard operating procedures and decision guidelines for the core finance and legal processes used by product, engineering, and GTM partners: budgeting & forecasting, contracts & legal process, procurement & vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and partnering teams to ensure consistent controls, predictable cadence, and compliance with accounting rules (ASC 606) and contractual obligations.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood legal entities and central finance activities (hosted API revenue, Dedicated/Private contracts, Marketplace sales).
- Includes operating thresholds for approvals, contract routing, procurement delegation, and revenue recognition triggers.

Key Contacts & Ownership:
- Finance owner: Claire Morgan (Finance Controller) – primary owner for budgeting, forecasting, and revrec guidance.
- Legal owner: Daniel Kim (Senior Counsel) – primary owner for contract templates, negotiation policy, and exceptions.
- Procurement owner: Priya Ramesh (Head of Procurement) – vendor onboarding, PO process, and vendor master data.
- Billing & AR owner: Evan Li (Revenue Accounting Manager) – invoicing cadence, collections, and accruals.

1) Budgeting & Forecasting (Quarterly and Rolling 12):
Purpose: Provide a single source of truth for resource allocation, capacity commitments (Dedicated), and runway planning.

Cadence and Deliverables:
1. Annual planning (Nov–Jan): CFO-led bottom-up budgets due to finance by second Friday of January. Deliverables: department budget workbook, headcount requests, capital requests.
2. Quarterly reforecast (within 3 weeks of quarter start): Updated revenue/expense forecast and headcount changes.
3. Monthly OP review: Actuals vs. forecast with variance analysis > 5% flagged to FP&A.

Approval & Thresholds:
- Department managers approve budgets up to $250k Opex.
- VP-level approval required for new programs > $250k and any capital expense > $50k.
- Executive Committee approval required for headcount plans that increase FTEs by > 10% of org headcount or > $1M incremental run-rate.

Modeling assumptions & templates:
- Use the canonical finance model (file: /finance/models/redwood-forecast-v3.xlsx).
- Assumptions to capture: ARR growth rate by product (hosted/dedicated/private), churn assumptions, average contract value (ACV), committed capacity uplift, estimated GPU spend by sku.

2) Contracts & Legal Process (Commercial / Customer / Supplier):
Purpose: Standardize contracting lifecycle to reduce cycle time and risk.

Standard Templates & Where to Find Them:
- Master Services Agreement (MSA) – standard customer MSA (redwood-msa-v4.docx).
- Statement of Work (SOW) – per-deployment SOW templates with SLAs and acceptance criteria.
- Vendor Agreement – procurement-side template with data protection addendum.
- NDA – mutual and one-way templates.

Routing & Approval Matrix:
1. Commercial contracts < $250k and standard terms: Sales to use standard MSA/SOW; Legal review optional; Sales Ops to execute.
2. Commercial contracts >= $250k or non-standard terms (data residency, indemnity caps, IP carve-outs): Legal review required; Legal routing doc to counsel for negotiation; CFO approval if revenue > $2M ACV or > 3 year term.
3. Any contract with non-standard data controls, security exceptions, or cross-border data transfers: Security & Privacy must sign off before execution.

Contract Redlines and Escalation Steps (numbered procedure):
1. Sales negotiates using the playbook exhibit and logs redlines in Contract Tracker (Confluence link).
2. If redlines are standard commercial items (price, term, SLA credits), Sales Ops and Legal standard negotiator can accept.
3. If redlines include liability > $500k, IP assignment changes, or novel indemnities, escalate to Legal Director + CFO for approval.
4. All executed contracts must be uploaded to the Contract Repository (DocStore) within 3 business days and tagged with customer_id and contract_type.

3) Procurement & Vendor Onboarding:
Purpose: Ensure vetted suppliers, approved spend, and clear PO practices to control cost and contractual risk.

Vendor Classification & Approval Tiers:
- Tier 1 (Strategic / > $250k annually): Legal contract, security review, exec sponsor, Procurement-led RFP recommended.
- Tier 2 ($25k–$250k annually): Standard vendor onboarding form, Finance PO, legal standard vendor agreement optional.
- Tier 3 (< $25k annually): Procurement card (P-card) or ad-hoc purchase; Procurement oversight on aggregated spend.

Procurement Workflow (PO-based purchases):
1. Requisition submitted in ProcureTool with GL code and business justification.
2. Manager approval -> Procurement review -> Finance PO issuance.
3. Vendor receives PO; goods/services delivered; AP processes invoice against PO.
4. Three-way match required for goods: PO, invoice, receiving confirmation.

Vendor Security & Data Handling:
- Any vendor with access to customer data or production environments must pass Security Questionnaire and sign Data Processing Addendum (DPA).
- On-prem or private deployment vendors must comply with our packaging & onprem third-party controls checklist (see Appendix A).

Escalations & Exceptions:
- Emergency purchases (e.g., critical hardware replacement) can be approved by Head of Infrastructure + Finance Controller; a PO must be created retroactively within 5 business days.

Vendor Master & Payments:
- Procurement maintains vendor master with required fields (tax id, payment terms, primary contact).
- Standard payment terms: Net 30. Exceptions (Net 45/60) require Finance VP approval. Early-payment discounts evaluated and recorded in treasury workflow.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies (Summary / Key Rules):
Purpose: Align billing practices with ASC 606 revenue recognition and ensure timely invoicing, collections, and deferred revenue management.

Recognition triggers by product:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue as usage occurs (variable consideration). Estimate and update monthly; use expected value for reporting when reliable.
- Dedicated (capacity commitment): Recognize ratably over the committed period once customer has access to reserved capacity and acceptance criteria are met. For multi-period contracts, allocate transaction price to performance obligations (capacity + support).
- Private / On-prem license + services: License revenue may be recognized at delivery if control transfers and acceptance criteria documented; professional services recognized over time based on labor hours or output method as contracted.

Billing cadence and invoicing rules:
- Standard approach: Invoice monthly in arrears for usage billing, or upfront for committed capacity (recognized as deferred revenue and amortized over the period).
- For prepayments or deposits, record as deferred revenue and move to recognized revenue according to performance obligations.
- All invoices must include: customer legal name, invoice date, contract ref, billing period, line-level charge description, tax details, and payment instructions.

Credit & Collections:
- Payment terms default: Net 30. Late fees assessed per contract.
- Collections workflow: D+1: automated reminder; D+15: AR Owner outreach; D+30: account hold warning; D+60: suspend non-essential services (after Legal sign-off); D+90: collections agency or litigation consideration.

Revenue Cutoff & Month-End Close Controls:
- Cutoff rule: Revenue recognized for usage during the reporting period regardless of billing date. Usage must be reconciled to billing system by Revenue Accounting within 5 business days of month close.
- Deferred revenue roll-forward and contract asset/liability reconciliation to be prepared and reviewed by Revenue Accounting and FP&A monthly.

Sample Journal Entries (text examples):
- Invoice for prepaid committed capacity: Debit Cash, Credit Deferred Revenue (liability). Monthly recognition: Debit Deferred Revenue, Credit Revenue.
- Usage billing invoice: Debit AR, Credit Revenue (if usage already delivered). Allowance for doubtful accounts booked as required.

Audit & Controls:
- Supporting documentation (contracts, SOWs, PO, usage logs) must be retained in the Contract Repository and Finance document store for 7 years.
- Revenue accounting procedures map to ASC 606; external audit checklist updated annually.

Appendices (quick references):
Appendix A — Onprem / Private deployment vendor controls checklist:
- Security questionnaire completed (yes/no).
- DPA executed (yes/no).
- KMS/HSM key access requirements documented (yes/no).
- Network segregation and runbook provided (yes/no).

Appendix B — Approval Matrix (summary table):
| Item | Threshold | Required Approvals |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Opex budget line | <= $250k | Department Manager |
| New program | > $250k | VP + Finance Controller |
| Capital spend | > $50k | VP Finance + Exec Committee |
| Commercial contract | >= $250k | Legal review + Sales Director |
| Vendor Tier 1 onboarding | > $250k/yr | Procurement + Legal + Security + Exec Sponsor |

Appendix C — Contract Lifecycle Checklist (to be completed before signature):
1. Confirm contract template and version.
2. Security & Privacy sign-off (if applicable).
3. Financial terms verified (billing cadence, taxes, currency).
4. Legal review/escalation completed.
5. Contract uploaded to repository and tagged.

How to request exceptions:
- Submit a change request in the Finance Exception queue with business justification, estimated dollar impact, and mitigation plan. Exceptions require sign-off by Finance Controller and Legal Counsel; Exec Committee for > $1M impact.
